column3: The people who left Egypt are referred to by a pronoun rather than explicitly named again as Israelites.
“Lift the head” and “by their skulls” retain the body images behind taking a census.
The Hebrew describes those going out to the army rather than explicitly saying they can serve.
The family is a house of fathers, retaining the ancestral expression.
The men are to stand with you rather than explicitly assist you.
The heads are over Israel’s thousands rather than explicitly clans.
Recording ancestry is grammatically attributed to those being counted.
